kumazaki2022.note: Cadaveric moment-arm study that treats psoas major and iliacus separately; both act as hip flexors. Neither this paper nor the project's muscle data gives a hip ADDUCTION action for iliacus (searched 2026-10-25: PubMed, web) -- iliacus adduction is therefore not animated.
kumazaki2022.quote: The iliopsoas (psoas major and iliacus), rectus femoris, sartorius, and adductor longus are known as the hip flexor muscles.

cp.f: Fibers run inferolaterally from occiput/upper cervical spine to the lateral clavicle/acromion; classically described as elevating the scapula, though Johnson et al.'s dissection study argues this transverse-ish fiber orientation contributes to scapular rotation mainly once rotation (driven by lower trapezius + serratus anterior) is already underway, rather than acting as a simple independent elevator.
Fibers run purely transversely (horizontally) from thoracic spinous processes to the acromion/scapular spine; the muscle's pure retractor component.

Fibers run superolaterally from lower thoracic spinous processes to the medial scapular spine; the standard teaching model describes this depressing the scapula and, paired with the upper part, forming a force couple producing upward rotation -- though per Johnson et al.'s dissection findings, the more precise mechanism is that the lower fibers isometrically fix the scapula's medial border so serratus anterior can drive the actual rotation.
